intro: Kansas runs its elections county by county, through each county election officer, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Show a photo ID to vote in person, such as a Kansas or other state driver's license or ID, a U.S. passport, a military ID, a tribal ID, a government employee ID, a Kansas college student ID, or a concealed carry license. Voters age 65 or older may use an expired photo ID.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: Registration books close 21 days before the election. Registrations received after this date are not processed until after the election.

dates.label: Advance voting
dates.detail: Advance ballots by mail are sent starting Oct. 14. In-person advance voting must begin in every county by Oct. 27, and each county sets its own start date, days and hours. In-person voting at county election offices ends at noon on Monday, Nov. 2.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm. State law says a mail ballot must be received by the close of polls. A court order currently requires ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if they arrive by the last mail delivery on Friday, Nov. 6. Ask your county election office which rule it follows.
